label: copy phase: input v (fed back) while outputting m, i.e. the original bigram v->m, at recall position >= 3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input is v and the token being output is m, so the original sequence contained the bigram v m. It needs recall_idx >= 3: it is silent when the v m pair sits at original positions 0-1 and almost silent at recall_idx 2 (19 activations). The strongest activations (about 2.1-2.6) are v m pairs late in long sequences. It never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, and never on a first occurrence of the input token. Weak residual activations (about 15% of activation mass) occur on copy-phase v inputs followed by other outputs, and on copy-phase m inputs whose output is also m (the original m m). Dev: precision 0.91, recall 0.64, mass recall 0.85; the missed activations are mostly in the lowest quartile.

issues: Minor: the claim 'never fires on a first occurrence of the input token' is trivially true. In the copy phase every input has already appeared in the original phase, so in_first is always 0 there.

Missed activations: 943 test steps holding 14% of activation mass. They are mostly weak and spread out: copy-phase v followed by an output other than m (22% of active steps, 8.7% of mass, precision only about 1%), and m->m (12% of active steps, 5% of mass, precision 10%). I found no token, position or history subclass that can be added without losing a lot of precision. Adding v with next_out==m reaches only 16% precision, and v->v reaches 7%.

False positives: 176 of 1960 predicted steps. They are slightly more common when v repeats in the original sequence (precision 0.82 with in_count>=2, against 0.93 with in_count==1). That difference is small and not a clean class.
F1 is 0.76, below 0.8. The verdict relies on mass recall (0.86) and precision (0.91). Activation-quartile coverage of 0.23 / 0.54 / 0.87 / 0.98 supports the claim that the misses are low-magnitude.
